legal_authority: Tax Reform Code Article XXIX-D; 72 P.S. § 9931-D
networking_equipment: Named: networking equipment, switches, racks, cabling, trays, and conduits
software: All software, including enabling software and licensing agreements
replacements_and_upgrades: Covered: the definition includes component parts, installations, refreshments, and replacements
power_and_cooling: Covered: power transformation and distribution equipment, generators, batteries, cooling systems, cooling towers, and air handling units
notable_exclusions: Telecommunications providers' data centers; equipment used to generate electricity for resale; local sales tax
qualification_threshold: $75M or $100M capital investment by county size; servers, networking equipment, and software do not count toward the threshold
status_2026: In effect; House passed repeal (HB 2198) 197-5 in June 2026 and the Senate passed repeal language in a separate bill, but neither was enacted; new applicants must meet the GRID Requirements (EO 2026-05)

networking_equipment: Named: servers, routers, connections, and other enabling hardware
software: Enabling software when sold or leased with exempt equipment; software sold separately is taxable
replacements_and_upgrades: Covered: purchases to upgrade, supplement, or replace equipment from the initial investment
power_and_cooling: Covered: chillers and backup generators by statute; Tax Commissioner rulings extend to power distribution and environmental control equipment
qualification_threshold: $150M investment and 50 jobs; $70M and 10 jobs in distressed localities
status_2026: In effect through June 30, 2035; Joint Subcommittee on Tax Policy review due Dec. 15, 2026

legal_authority: Ohio Rev. Code § 122.175; Ohio Admin. Code 122:28-1-02
networking_equipment: Not named; covered as tangible personal property used to conduct a computer data center business
software: Prewritten software used to operate, manage, or maintain the data center; excludes accounting, payroll, and HR software
replacements_and_upgrades: Set in each agreement; the statute's capital investment definition includes replacement and repair
power_and_cooling: Covered: equipment cooling systems, property that generates, transforms, or distributes electricity, and redundant power supply equipment
notable_exclusions: Property not part of the data center business, such as office furniture and general business software
qualification_threshold: $100M investment over three years and $1.5M annual payroll
status_2026: New applications paused since May 27, 2026; Substitute HB 646 would cut new exemptions to 50% and is expected to return after the November election

networking_equipment: Named in state guidance: network infrastructure, alongside servers, mainframes, and data storage
replacements_and_upgrades: Covered in effect: the exemption applies to property purchased or leased to establish or operate a data center, throughout the annually renewed certificate period
power_and_cooling: Covered: heating, ventilation, air-conditioning, and mechanical systems, and equipment to generate, transform, transmit, distribute, or manage electricity
qualification_threshold: $2M (Tier 1 area) or $5M elsewhere, and 5 qualified positions
status_2026: In effect; governor seeking repeal in the 2027 session

networking_equipment: Named: switches, routers, wiring, and cabling
replacements_and_upgrades: Covered: certificate holders may make exempt purchases through Dec. 31, 2031, and the Department of Revenue lists components and repair or replacement parts as included
power_and_cooling: Covered: emergency backup generators, air handling units, cooling towers, energy storage, power distribution units, switching gear, and batteries
notable_exclusions: None identified; covers both state and local sales tax
qualification_threshold: $250M, $75M, or $25M by county population, plus quality jobs, over a seven-year investment period
status_2026: In effect through Dec. 31, 2031; 2026 bills to repeal or end it early did not pass
